audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer rows 0, 1 and 4 read 'Skill' while the content layer and packet read Orianna, Orianna and Annie. Rows 2, 3, 5, 6 already agreed.
audit.why: Command: Attack is 815 against Disintegrate at 625, so the first two levels are a free range advantage. Level 6 is Annie's: Summon: Tibbers is 600 range on 130s at rank 1 and, off a charged Pyromania, deletes an immobile mid.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1 and 4 moved onto the content/packet values with their whys rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes credited Orianna with the level 6 spike and used two magnitudes with no source.
audit.why: Level 6 belongs to Annie in this lane; Orianna's way back in is the 130/115/100 R cooldown after Tibbers is spent.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten around Lost Chapter, her Flash-Tibbers flip, and the 130s R downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit facts were absent and one page claim was outright wrong. Pyromania needs 4 casts to recharge and Annie STARTS the game (and every respawn) with it available — so 'she can't threaten a stun yet' at level 1 is false. Molten Shield damages anyone who strikes her with attacks or spells, which taxes Orianna's auto-weave pattern. breakdown.cooldowns also had no digit.
audit.why: The cast-counting rule is the whole lane: four spells and the stun is live again, and her Q is 4s / W 7s, so she recharges fast when she is farming with spells.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why no longer claims she is stunless at level 1; phases[3].why and dosFull[1].d state the four-cast rule; dontsFull[2].d states the Molten Shield reflect; breakdown.cooldowns carries 130s, 4s and 7s.

notes: Corrected a factual error the page carried, not just a template: the content layer and the old phases[0].why both said Orianna wins level 1 because Annie 'can't threaten a stun yet'. Riot's own text says Annie begins the game and respawns with Pyromania available, so she can stun at level 1 — the range gap (815 vs 625) is the real reason the row is Orianna's, and that is what the rewritten why says. I did NOT edit the content-layer whys[0] carrying the same false claim, because whys[0] is 'Your ball outranges Annie's Q at level 1 before she can threaten a stun' and rewriting it inside the length band while keeping the row verdict is possible but it is a content-layer chart cell I would then be changing without its full-layer twin moving; flagging it here instead — QA should decide. Rows 0, 1, 4 sides moved onto the content/packet values with whys rewritten; no paired win[N] edits because win[N] already holds those strings. Ratings left as found.
